message.content: The most well‑known dominant genetic trait in lions is the **presence of a mane in adult male lions**. In the wild, the mane is a sexually selected trait that signals health and dominance. Genetic studies suggest that the mane is largely controlled by a dominant allele (or set of alleles) that is expressed in males but not in females. This means that if a male lion inherits the allele from either parent, he will develop a mane, whereas females do not express it regardless of genotype.
